scope: Only CodeQL alert 48 reachability; read-only product source and existing GitHub analysis

findings.statement: The assignment at1226 is inside typeof metadata[key] === "number". Missing keys use the separate Map-backed eval cache; nonnumeric values return without assigning metadata.

The only numeric erased-type metadata initializer in this bundle is compiler-owned JSON {e8:1,ho:2,aG:1,fx:2,cj:1,u9:1}. These six keys are disjoint from __proto__, constructor, prototype and other inherited object property names.
The only call site for A.w0 passes effectiveConstructor.name. String fields in Uri/database/query data are not copied into a constructor name.

instanceType uses compiler Dart class constructors or interceptors. Plain structured-clone shapes are handled by fixed JS-object interceptors; an own constructor:{name:...} data field is not used as their Dart class constructor.
The metadata uses ordinary object literals, not null-prototype objects. Safety at this sink comes from the numeric-probe branch and compiler-owned key set, not a nonexistent null-prototype defense.

findings.evidence: Existing SARIF analysis1959431365 has four paths, all starting at self.location.href and ending after a.constructor / effectiveConstructor.name.
findings.statement: The taint path conflates the data content of URI/list/map instances with their compiler-owned constructor identity. None of these four SARIF paths demonstrates rewriting the metadata key or its numeric-entry initializer.

The initialization event reads a fixed protocol type, then converts string fields and constructs compiled Dart message classes. Unknown types and nonstring database/URI fields reject. The Node cases invoke the real A.kw event adapter and parser; the handler after parsing is intercepted to avoid database operations.

Legacy RPC deserialization converts cloned data to Dart values; modern RPC parsing constructs fixed compiled message types. Synthetic row/query-text shapes and modern error text were probed without executing SQL or touching browser storage.

This worker is selected by the web/js_interop database connection. Native Android/iOS use the ffi connection. This is not a waiver for the web asset or a claim that a signed app artifact was inspected.

proof.argument: For the exact hashed bundle and its unmodified compiler metadata, any execution of the reported assignment requires its property key to be one of six compiler-generated, non-prototype keys. Even arbitrary string-key control alone would not satisfy the assignment precondition for __proto__/constructor/prototype. URL and message data cannot change that key set through this sink. The bounded probes corroborate this argument and positively exercise all six numeric entries.
limits: Node VM is not a browser Worker/MessagePort or end-to-end SQLite test.
A diagnostic closure export was inserted in memory only; A.w0 itself was wrapped to observe calls and the metadata object was proxied to observe writes. Disk source stayed byte-identical.
Serve parser cases use inert object port placeholders and intercept the post-parse handler; no claim of valid native MessagePort behavior.
No network, SQL, browser storage, application account, production or privileged operation occurs in the probe.
This conclusion is pinned to this worker SHA and numeric initializer; compiler regeneration or SDK/dependency change requires revalidation.
No GitHub dismissal, suppression, CodeQL rescan or change of severity was performed.
assumptions: The worker runs with its pinned, unmodified compiler-owned metadata initializer.

No pre-existing arbitrary JavaScript execution or separate prototype-pollution vulnerability has changed the worker realm or runtime metadata. Such a separate compromise is not established by alert48.

decision.minimalProductFixRequiredForThisSink: None demonstrated; do not hand-edit generated JavaScript, suppress the rule, or introduce a broad dependency upgrade solely to silence this alert.
